hoisin.name: Hoisin sauce
hoisin.watch: Check the label for oyster or shrimp extract. Most hoisin has none.

tamari.name: Tamari
tamari.watch: Check the label: most tamari is gluten-free, but not every brand.

tortilla-flour.name: Flour tortillas (8-inch)
tortilla-flour.watch: Check the label for lard. Most store brands use oil or vegetable shortening instead.

tortilla-corn.name: Corn tortillas (6-inch)
tortilla-corn.watch: Check the label for lard. Most store brands don't use it.

sour-cream.name: Sour cream
sour-cream.watch: Check the label for gelatin. Pick a brand made without it.

cottage-cheese.name: Small-curd cottage cheese
cottage-cheese.watch: Check the label for gelatin. Pick a brand made without it.

beef-sirloin.name: Beef sirloin steak, about 1 inch thick

yogurt-greek.name: Plain Greek yogurt
yogurt-greek.watch: Check the label for gelatin. Pick a brand made without it.

refried-beans.name: Vegetarian refried beans
refried-beans.watch: Many refried beans are made with lard. Buy a can marked vegetarian, and check the label.

turkey-sausage-bulk.name: Bulk turkey breakfast sausage (no casing)
turkey-sausage-bulk.watch: Buy bulk turkey sausage, sold loose with no casing. Links often use pork casings, even when the meat is turkey.

tortilla-burrito.name: Burrito-size flour tortillas (10-inch)
tortilla-burrito.watch: Check the label for lard. Most store brands use oil or vegetable shortening instead.

tortilla-gluten-free.name: Gluten-free tortillas
tortilla-gluten-free.watch: Check the label for lard. Most store brands use oil or vegetable shortening instead.

turkey-strips.name: Turkey bacon
turkey-strips.watch: Pick a package that says fully cooked.

chicken-sausage-smoked.name: Smoked chicken andouille sausage (fully cooked)
chicken-sausage-smoked.watch: Buy chicken andouille that's collagen-cased or skinless. Many chicken sausages are stuffed into pork casings, and some mix in pork, so read the whole label. Beef kielbasa works too, with the same checks.

beef-kielbasa.name: Beef kielbasa (fully cooked)
beef-kielbasa.watch: Buy kielbasa labeled all beef, collagen-cased or skinless. Most kielbasa is pork, and many beef ones still use pork casings, so read the whole label.

noodles-wheat.name: Thin wheat noodles (Shanghai or plain lo mein)
noodles-wheat.watch: Check the label: some fresh noodles have egg. Either kind works.

nori.name: Roasted seaweed sheets (nori, for kimbap or sushi)
nori.watch: Buy plain sheets. Seasoned snack packs can have fish flavoring.

bolillo-rolls.watch: Check the label for lard. Most bakery rolls use oil or shortening.
bolillo-rolls.name: Bolillo rolls (or small French rolls)

rotisserie-chicken.watch: Buy a plain or lemon-herb chicken. Check the label: no bacon or ham in the seasoning.
rotisserie-chicken.name: Rotisserie chicken

fish-sauce.watch: Check the label: anchovies, salt, and sugar only. Some brands add shrimp or squid; skip those.
fish-sauce.name: Fish sauce

gochujang.watch: Check the label: most are rice, chili, soybeans, and salt. Skip any with shrimp or squid.
gochujang.name: Gochujang (Korean chili paste)

tostada-shells.name: Tostada shells
tostada-shells.watch: Check the label: some tostada shells are fried in lard. Most brands use vegetable oil, and baked ones use none.

edamame-frozen.name: Frozen shelled edamame or baby lima beans

beef-dry-sausage.name: Beef salami
beef-dry-sausage.watch: Check the label: all beef, in a collagen or cellulose casing. Many salami casings are pork, even on beef salami.

bresaola.name: Bresaola (air-dried beef), sliced
bresaola.watch: Check the label: beef only. Some deli counters slice it beside prosciutto, so buy it sealed.

labneh.name: Labneh (strained yogurt)
labneh.watch: Check the label for gelatin. Or strain plain Greek yogurt overnight to make your own.

chicken-ready-cut.name: Ready-cut chicken breast, plain (chunks or stir-fry strips)

taco-shells.name: Hard taco shells
taco-shells.watch: Check the label: some taco shells are fried in lard. Most brands use vegetable oil.

quail-whole.name: Whole quail
quail-whole.watch: Most stores sell quail frozen, four to a pack. Thaw them in the fridge overnight.

snapper-whole.name: Whole red snapper, scaled and gutted
snapper-whole.watch: Ask the fish counter to scale and gut it. Check the label says red snapper: some fish sold as snapper is another kind.

apple-tart.name: Tart baking apples (Granny Smith or Honeycrisp)

tweezers.name: Clean tweezers or needle-nose pliers (for fish bones)

pot-large.name: Large heavy pot with a lid (like a Dutch oven)

shallow-dish.name: Wide shallow dish, like a pie plate

heatproof-bowl.name: Heatproof glass or metal bowl that sits on top of the saucepan

skewers.name: Skewers, metal or wooden (soak wooden ones 30 minutes)

pie-weights.name: Pie weights, or 2 cups of dried beans kept for baking

building-a-sauce.name: Building a sauce
building-a-sauce.idea: Layer flavor in one pan: fat, aromatics, spices, liquid, then simmer it down.

poaching-eggs.name: Gentle eggs
poaching-eggs.idea: Low, steady heat sets eggs all the way through without turning them rubbery.

thin-slicing.name: Thin slicing
thin-slicing.idea: Thin slices across the grain cook fast and stay tender.

marinating.name: Marinating
marinating.idea: A salty, sweet, or tangy soak flavors meat before it ever hits the pan.

cutting-in-fat.name: Cutting in cold fat
cutting-in-fat.idea: Little pieces of cold butter turn to steam in the oven and puff dough into flaky layers.

folding-layers.name: Folding for layers
folding-layers.idea: Folding dough over itself stacks the butter into thin layers.

browning-butter.name: Browning butter
browning-butter.idea: Cooking butter past melted toasts its milk solids and makes it taste nutty.

creaming.name: Creaming
creaming.idea: Beating soft butter with sugar traps air, and that air makes baked things softer and lighter.

julienne.name: Julienne
julienne.idea: Cut food into thin matchsticks so it cooks fast and rolls up neatly.

fine-chopping.name: Fine chopping
fine-chopping.idea: Chop herbs and vegetables into small, even bits so every bite gets some.

dicing.name: Dicing
dicing.idea: Cut into small cubes, all about the same size, so they cook evenly.

rolling-wrapping.name: Rolling and wrapping
rolling-wrapping.idea: Fill a wrapper snugly and roll it tight so it holds together.

dressings.name: Whisked dressings
dressings.idea: Whisking oil into something tangy makes a dressing that clings to food.

quick-pickling.name: Quick pickling
quick-pickling.idea: A hot vinegar brine turns crisp vegetables tangy in under an hour.

searing.name: High-heat searing
searing.idea: A very hot pan browns the outside fast, and browning is flavor.

broiling.name: Broiling
broiling.idea: Strong heat from above cooks thin food fast and chars the top.

heat-control.name: Heat control
heat-control.idea: Turning the heat up or down at the right time is most of cooking.

stir-frying.name: Stir-frying
stir-frying.idea: Small pieces, a very hot pan, and constant moving cook food in minutes.

simmering.name: Simmering
simmering.idea: Small, lazy bubbles cook gently without toughening food.

braising.name: Braising
braising.idea: Brown first, then cook slowly in a little liquid until tender.

reducing.name: Reducing
reducing.idea: Boiling off water makes a sauce thicker and its flavor stronger.

emulsions.name: Emulsions
emulsions.idea: Fat and water mix into a smooth sauce when you add them slowly and keep stirring.

crisping.name: Crisping
crisping.idea: Dry food and hot fat make a crunchy, golden crust.

timing.name: Timing a meal
timing.idea: Start the slowest part first so everything is ready together.

roux.name: Roux
roux.idea: Flour cooked in butter thickens milk or broth into a smooth sauce.

blooming-spices.name: Blooming spices
blooming-spices.idea: Spices wake up in hot fat, so a minute in the oil makes them taste stronger.

flavor-base.name: Flavor base
flavor-base.idea: Onions and their friends cooked slowly build the flavor everything else sits on.

spice-rubs.name: Spice rubs
spice-rubs.idea: A dry mix of spices rubbed on before cooking seasons the outside.

one-pot-stews.name: One-pot stews
one-pot-stews.idea: Build a whole meal in one pot, adding each part when it needs the time.

layering.name: Building in layers
layering.idea: Make each part well on its own, then stack them so every bite has all of them.

breaking-down-chicken.name: Breaking down a chicken
breaking-down-chicken.idea: Cutting a whole bird into pieces saves money and gives bones for stock.

making-stock.name: Making stock
making-stock.idea: Bones and vegetables simmered for hours make a broth with real flavor.

shredding.name: Shredding
shredding.idea: Meat braised until tender pulls apart into strands that soak up sauce.

masa-dough.name: Masa dough
masa-dough.idea: Corn masa mixed with water makes a dough you press and griddle.

pleating.name: Pleating and sealing
pleating.idea: Small folds seal a filling inside a wrapper so it stays put while cooking.

flatbreads.name: Flatbreads
flatbreads.idea: A soft dough rolled thin cooks in minutes in a very hot pan.

scalded-dough.name: Cooked doughs
scalded-dough.idea: Stirring flour or starch into hot liquid makes a dough that puffs and stays chewy.

muffin-method.name: The muffin method
muffin-method.idea: Mix wet and dry separately, then stir together only until just combined.

skillet-baking.name: Skillet baking
skillet-baking.idea: A preheated cast-iron pan gives batter a crisp, golden bottom.

yeast-dough.name: Yeast dough
yeast-dough.idea: Kneading builds stretch, and yeast fills the dough with air as it rises.

batters.name: Batters
batters.idea: A thin batter poured hot sets into crêpes, cakes, or a crisp coating.

filling-crimping.name: Filling and crimping
filling-crimping.idea: Fold dough over a filling and press the edge so nothing leaks.

stiff-porridge.name: Cornmeal porridge
stiff-porridge.idea: Stirring cornmeal into boiling water until it pulls from the pan makes a dough you eat by hand.

pastry.name: Pastry
pastry.idea: Cold butter, cold water, and a light touch make a crust that is crisp and tender.

layered-pastry.name: Phyllo
layered-pastry.idea: Paper-thin sheets brushed with fat bake into crackly layers.

custards.name: Custards
custards.idea: Eggs and milk baked gently set smooth instead of curdling.

breading-frying.name: Breading and shallow frying
breading-frying.idea: Flour, egg, crumbs, then hot oil a finger deep makes a crunchy crust.

deep-frying.name: Deep frying
deep-frying.idea: Food fried in oil at the right temperature cooks through and stays crisp, not greasy.

oven-browning.name: Oven browning
oven-browning.idea: Dry heat in the oven browns and crisps, with a stir partway for even color.

binders.name: Binders
binders.idea: Egg and crumbs hold ground meat together so it slices instead of crumbling.

roasting.name: Roasting and carving
roasting.idea: Roast, rest so the juices settle, then carve across the grain.

gravy.name: Pan gravy
gravy.idea: The browned bits in a roasting pan become gravy with a little flour and broth.

cooking-legumes.name: Cooking dried beans and lentils
cooking-legumes.idea: Dried beans and lentils simmer gently until they're soft all the way through; lentils need no soaking, beans cook faster after one.

temping-meat.name: Checking meat with a thermometer
temping-meat.idea: The only way to know ground meat is safe is to check the middle: 160°F for beef, 165°F for poultry.

sauteing.name: Sautéing
sauteing.idea: A hot pan and shimmering oil cook small pieces fast, so they brown outside before they go soft.

cooking-grains.name: Cooking grains
cooking-grains.idea: Grains drink a set amount of liquid; toast them first and leave the lid on, and every grain stays separate.

handling-poultry.name: Handling raw poultry
handling-poultry.idea: Raw chicken goes on its own board, never gets rinsed, and is followed by washing hands and everything it touched.

cooking-fish.name: Cooking fish
cooking-fish.idea: Fish is delicate and cooks fast; it's done when it turns opaque and flakes, at 145°F.

building-soup.name: Building a soup
building-soup.idea: A soup is built in layers: a base, a good stock, and seasoning tasted at every stage.

blanching.name: Blanching
blanching.idea: A quick dip in boiling water, then straight into ice water, keeps a vegetable bright and crisp and stops it cooking.

cooling-reheating.name: Cooling and reheating
cooling-reheating.idea: Cooked food cools fast in shallow containers, goes in the fridge within 2 hours, and is reheated to 165°F.

knife-safety.name: Knife grip and safety
knife-safety.idea: A steady board, a bridge or claw grip, and a sharp knife keep fingers safe.

mise-en-place.name: Setting out first
mise-en-place.idea: Read the recipe through and set out every ingredient and tool before the heat goes on.

measuring.name: Measuring and scaling
measuring.idea: Level dry cups, read wet ones at eye level, and halve, double, or weigh a recipe to fit.

reading-labels.name: Reading labels
reading-labels.idea: Find the hidden unclean ingredients in a list before food goes in the cart.

steaming.name: Steaming
steaming.idea: Food cooks gently over boiling water, so it stays moist and keeps its color.

seasoning.name: Seasoning by taste
seasoning.idea: Add salt, acid, and spice a little at a time, tasting as you go.

grilling.name: Grilling over two zones
grilling.idea: A hot side sears and a cooler side cooks through, with the lid as an oven.

terms.means: Cut into small cubes about the size of a pea. Try to make them all close to the same size so they cook evenly.
Chop into tiny bits, smaller than a grain of rice. Keep rocking the knife back and forth over the pile until nothing big is left.
Cut into rough, bite-size pieces. They don't have to match.
Cut into flat pieces, like slices of bread.
Cut into thin sticks, about the size of a matchstick.
How chefs hold a knife: thumb and bent pointer finger pinch the blade just in front of the handle, and the other fingers wrap the handle. It steers the tip exactly where you aim.
How your other hand holds food for cutting: fingertips curled under, knuckles forward, and the flat of the blade resting against your knuckles. The knife can't reach your fingertips.
Run a knife's edge along a honing steel to push it back into line. It keeps a knife sharp between sharpenings, and you can do it every time you cook.
A flat slice cut the long way, the first step of a dice or julienne. Even planks make even sticks and cubes.
The finest dice: cubes about ⅛ inch on every side, cut from a julienne.
Sticks about ¼ inch thick and 2 to 3 inches long. Cut across, they make a small dice.
Leaves stacked, rolled up tight, and sliced across into thin ribbons. Used for basil, mint, and greens.
Rub food down a grater so it falls off in shreds. The big holes make shreds. The small holes make a paste.
Grate just the colored outside of a lemon or orange peel. Stop when you see white; the white part tastes bitter.
Cook a liquid with small, lazy bubbles that pop now and then. If big bubbles roll all over, turn the heat down.
Big bubbles rolling all over the pot, even while you stir.
Cook gently in liquid that's barely bubbling.
Cook in a little hot oil or butter, stirring often.
Cook in a very hot pan without moving the food, so the outside turns deep brown.
Brown the food first, then cook it slowly with a little liquid and the lid on until it's very tender.
Soak food in a flavorful liquid, called a marinade, before you cook it.
Stir fast in little circles with a whisk or a fork, to mix things together and add air.
Beat soft butter and sugar together hard until the mixture is fluffy and a little paler.
Lay the dough over itself in layers, like folding a letter to fit in an envelope.
Push the dough away with the heel of your hand, fold it back, turn it, and repeat until it's smooth and stretchy.
Let shaped dough rise a second time before it bakes, until it's puffy and a gentle poke springs back slowly.
Wake an ingredient up before it goes in. Yeast blooms in warm water until it foams, which shows it's alive. Spices bloom in hot oil until they smell strong.
Dough that has just come together: rough, lumpy, and sticky, with dry bits still showing. Kneading turns it smooth.
Slightly sticky. A tacky dough grabs your finger for a moment, then lets go clean, without leaving dough behind.
Stretch a small piece of dough slowly between your fingers. If it goes thin enough to see light through without tearing, it's kneaded enough.
A beaten egg, often with a spoonful of water, brushed on dough before baking so the crust turns shiny and golden.
Press a floured fingertip into rising dough. If the dent springs back slowly and leaves a small mark, it's ready to bake. Springs back fast: wait longer. Doesn't spring back: it's gone too far.
The soft inside of a bread or cake, and the pattern of holes you see when you slice it.
A yeast dough made richer with fat, eggs, sugar, or milk, like challah or dinner rolls. It bakes softer and browns faster than a lean dough of flour, water, yeast, and salt.
Sprinkle a thin, light layer, like flour on the counter so dough doesn't stick.
Gently lift and turn the food so every piece gets coated, like tossing a salad.
Hot oil looks wavy and rippled on top. That means it's hot enough for the food.
Meat has thin lines running through it, like the lines in wood. Cut across those lines, not along them, so each bite is tender.
Butter and flour cooked together, stirring, for a few minutes. It thickens milk or broth into a smooth sauce. Say it "roo."
Cook something for just a minute or two in boiling water, then scoop it straight into a bowl of ice water. The ice water stops the cooking, so it stays bright green and a little crunchy.
Pour a little liquid into a hot pan after browning, and scrape up the brown bits stuck to the bottom. They melt into the liquid and give the dish its deep, savory flavor.
Cook vegetables gently over medium-low heat, often with a pinch of salt, until they're soft and see-through but not brown.
The brown bits stuck to a pan after food browns. Golden to dark brown is flavor; black is burnt. Deglazing lifts it into the sauce.
Plunge just-cooked food into ice water to stop the cooking, so vegetables stay crisp and bright.
The temperature where a fat starts to smoke and break down. Past it, oil tastes harsh and can catch fire.
Strong-smelling vegetables, like onion, garlic, celery, and ginger, cooked first to build a dish's flavor.
France's flavor base: onion, carrot, and celery, about two parts onion to one part each of the others.
Italy's flavor base: onion, carrot, and celery chopped fine and cooked slowly in olive oil.
The Spanish and Latin American flavor base: onion, garlic, and peppers, often with tomato, cooked gently in oil.
A seed that grows in a pod: beans, lentils, peas, and chickpeas. Dried, they keep for a year or more.
Spread dried beans or lentils out and look through them, taking out any tiny stones, dirt, or shriveled ones.
Boil dried beans for 2 minutes, turn off the heat, cover them, and leave them an hour. It's almost as good as soaking overnight.
A full, rolling boil, with big bubbles across the whole pot. Red kidney beans need 10 minutes of it to be safe.
Cooking a grain in just enough liquid for it to drink all of it, so nothing is drained.
A grain toasted in fat before the liquid goes in, then cooked with the lid on until every grain is separate.
A boneless piece of fish cut from along the backbone, with or without its skin.
Thin, soft bones in a row down the thick end of a fish fillet. Feel for them with your fingertips and pull them out with tweezers.
Cook food in the hot, wet air above boiling water, with a lid on. The gentlest way to cook fish and vegetables.
When cooked fish is pressed with a fork, it separates into layers called flakes. Flaking is one sign fish is done.
Food sealed in folded parchment and baked, so it steams in its own juices. French cooks call it en papillote.
Make shallow cuts across the surface of food, often in a crosshatch, without cutting all the way through. It lets fat run out, flavor soak in, or heat reach the middle.
Cook something fatty slowly so its fat melts out and collects in the pan, leaving the skin or meat crisp.

Mix something gently into a batter by scooping the spatula down to the bottom of the bowl and turning the batter over on top, then giving the bowl a quarter turn. It mixes without stirring out the air or crushing soft pieces.

units.4: Breaking down and slicing meat, marinades

lessons.label: S1a
lessons.title: Fresh spring rolls
lessons.about: Soft rice-paper rolls filled with crunchy vegetables, chicken, noodles, and mint, dipped in a peanut-hoisin sauce. Served cool, not fried.

lessons.label: S1b
lessons.title: Chicken fajitas
lessons.skill: Julienne: peppers and onions in thin strips
lessons.about: Strips of seared chicken with peppers and onions, wrapped in warm tortillas with salsa and sour cream.

lessons.label: S1c
lessons.title: Baked shoestring fries
lessons.about: Thin, crispy potato sticks baked in the oven instead of fried.

lessons.label: S2a
lessons.title: Fattoush
lessons.about: A crunchy Lebanese salad of chopped vegetables, herbs, and toasted pita pieces in a lemony dressing.

lessons.label: S2b
lessons.title: Chimichurri steak
lessons.about: Seared steak topped with chimichurri, a bright Argentine sauce of chopped parsley, garlic, oregano, and vinegar.

lessons.label: S2c
lessons.title: Tuna salad sandwiches
lessons.skill: Fine chopping: celery, onion, pickles, herbs
lessons.about: Classic tuna salad with finely chopped celery, onion, pickles, and herbs, on bread.

lessons.label: S3a
lessons.title: Pico de gallo + Baja fish tacos
lessons.about: Broiled white fish in tortillas with fresh pico de gallo, a chunky salsa of diced tomato, onion, and cilantro.

lessons.label: S3b
lessons.title: Ratatouille
lessons.about: A French vegetable stew of diced eggplant, zucchini, peppers, and tomato, cooked slowly with herbs.

lessons.label: S3c
lessons.title: Minestrone
lessons.about: A hearty Italian vegetable soup with beans and small pasta.

lessons.label: S4a
lessons.title: Chicken Caesar + homemade dressing & croutons
lessons.about: Romaine salad with sliced chicken, a homemade creamy Caesar dressing, and crunchy homemade croutons.

lessons.label: S4b
lessons.title: Chicken souvlaki pitas
lessons.skill: A yogurt sauce, chopping herbs fine
lessons.about: Lemon and oregano chicken seared in a skillet and tucked into warm pitas with tomato, onion, and a cool cucumber-yogurt tzatziki.

lessons.label: S4c
lessons.title: Chickpea chopped salad + vinaigrette
lessons.skill: Whisking a vinaigrette, dressing to taste
lessons.about: A big chopped salad of romaine, cucumber, tomato, and chickpeas, tossed with a red wine vinaigrette whisked from scratch and tasted until it's balanced.

lessons.label: S5
lessons.title: Smash burgers + quick pickles
lessons.skill: Thin slicing, quick pickle, high-heat sear
lessons.about: Thin beef patties smashed onto a very hot pan for crispy edges, with quick homemade pickles.

lessons.label: S6a
lessons.title: French-style omelet
lessons.about: A soft, pale-yellow rolled omelet cooked gently over low heat. A breakfast dish.

lessons.label: S6b
lessons.title: Grilled cheese + tomato soup
lessons.about: Crispy, golden grilled cheese sandwiches with a smooth homemade tomato soup for dipping.

lessons.label: S6c
lessons.title: Challah French toast
lessons.about: Thick slices of challah soaked in a sweet egg custard and cooked golden. A breakfast dish.

lessons.label: S7
lessons.title: Crispy hash browns
lessons.about: Shredded potatoes squeezed dry and pan-fried into a crispy golden cake. A breakfast side.

lessons.label: S8a
lessons.title: Shakshuka
lessons.skill: Building a sauce, then poaching eggs in it
lessons.about: Eggs gently cooked in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce, served in the pan with bread for dipping.

lessons.label: S8b
lessons.title: Spaghetti marinara
lessons.about: Spaghetti in a simple homemade tomato sauce with garlic and basil.

lessons.label: S8c
lessons.title: Honey-garlic chicken
lessons.about: Bite-size chicken in a sticky, sweet-savory honey, garlic, and soy sauce, over rice.

lessons.label: S9a
lessons.title: Chicken fried rice
lessons.about: Day-old rice stir-fried fast with chicken, egg, vegetables, and soy sauce.

lessons.label: S9b
lessons.title: Turkey lettuce wraps
lessons.about: Ground turkey stir-fried with carrots, water chestnuts, and a hoisin sauce, spooned into cold lettuce cups.

lessons.label: S9c
lessons.title: Vegetable stir-fry with tofu
lessons.about: Carrots, peppers, and snow peas cut into thin matchsticks and stir-fried fast with crisp tofu in a garlic-ginger sauce, over rice.

lessons.label: S10
lessons.title: Oyakodon
lessons.about: A Japanese rice bowl of chicken and onion simmered in a sweet soy broth, with egg set gently on top.

lessons.label: S11a
lessons.title: Chicken adobo
lessons.about: Filipino chicken braised in vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, and bay leaves until tender, then glazed. Served with rice.

lessons.label: S11b
lessons.title: Chicken piccata
lessons.about: Thin chicken cutlets seared golden, in a bright lemon and caper pan sauce made in the same skillet.

lessons.label: S11c
lessons.title: Pineapple teriyaki salmon
lessons.about: Seared salmon under a shiny homemade teriyaki glaze of pineapple juice and soy, with warm pineapple and rice.

lessons.label: S12
lessons.title: Breakfast burritos
lessons.about: Flour tortillas rolled around scrambled eggs, crispy potatoes, beef or turkey sausage, and cheese.

lessons.label: S13
lessons.title: Cacio e pepe
lessons.about: Roman pasta with a creamy sauce made only from cheese, black pepper, and starchy pasta water.

lessons.label: S14a
lessons.title: Eggs Benedict
lessons.about: Poached eggs on toasted English muffins with turkey bacon or smoked salmon, under a buttery hollandaise sauce.

lessons.label: S14b
lessons.title: Huevos rancheros
lessons.about: Eggs cooked in simmering salsa, served on crisp corn tortillas with refried beans. A breakfast or supper dish.

lessons.label: S15a
lessons.title: Stovetop mac and cheese
lessons.skill: Roux, then béchamel, then cheese sauce
lessons.about: Creamy macaroni in a homemade cheese sauce, made on the stove.

lessons.label: S15b
lessons.title: Chicken and spinach crêpes
lessons.about: Thin French pancakes wrapped around chicken and spinach in a creamy white sauce.

lessons.label: S15c
lessons.title: Japanese chicken curry
lessons.skill: Roux with curry powder, from scratch
lessons.about: A mild, thick Japanese curry with chicken, potatoes, and carrots over rice. The curry sauce is made from scratch.

lessons.label: S16a
lessons.title: Chana masala
lessons.about: An Indian chickpea curry in a spiced onion and tomato sauce, with rice.

lessons.label: S18b
lessons.title: Red lentil soup (mercimek)
lessons.skill: Cooking lentils until they melt, blending a soup
lessons.about: Turkish red lentil soup: lentils simmered with onion, carrot, and a little tomato until soft, blended smooth, and finished with lemon and a paprika butter.

lessons.label: S19
lessons.title: Red beans and rice
lessons.skill: Soaking dried beans, simmering them until creamy
lessons.about: A Louisiana dish of red beans soaked overnight and simmered until creamy with onion, celery, and green pepper and smoked beef sausage, over rice.

lessons.label: S20b
lessons.title: Chicken jambalaya
lessons.skill: An onion, celery, and pepper base, deglazing, rice cooked in the pot
lessons.about: Louisiana one-pot rice: chicken and smoked chicken andouille browned, onion, celery, and green pepper sweated, the pot deglazed, and the rice cooked in the flavorful broth.

lessons.label: S22a
